Marta — thanks for the packet and the matrix. I've pulled in Kimberly (Contracts) and Evelyn (Legal Ops). A few quick notes and proposed next steps:  

1) Intake owner: I'll be the intake owner for Redwood — I'll collect initial party data and route to Contracts for a redline.
2) Template approach: In most cases we start from Redwood's standard MSA and apply counterparty redlines. That lets us validate template parity (which clauses must live in MSA vs Order Form exhibits). If Helix prefers to start from your MSA, we can do that but it often adds review time.
3) Party matrix: we need clearer billing contact (person + email) and service owner for the sandbox environment. Can you add two columns: "Redwood contact required" (yes/no) and "Regulatory residency" (US/EU/APAC) to the matrix?
4) Turnaround: we'll aim for a first-pass redline within 3 business days after we have full party contact info and confirmation on which template to start from. If Helix wants our template, I'll attach it to my next email.

Preference for document return: shared Drive + email summary works best. For signatures we'll use DocuSign at the end, not for redline iteration.

I'll attach Redwood's current MSA template and a short intake checklist in my next message.

Best,

- SLA redlines: we'll map your uptime credit structure to our standard Exhibit B template and call out any non-standard credit triggers.
- Timeline: target internal first-pass redline by Wed 2026-09-02 (EOD) assuming we have the completed party matrix (with billing contact + service owner) by tomorrow EOD. If any of the required contacts are missing we'll push the timeline and will notify you.
